title: PowerBI Platform Engineer
description:
About the Role

The Power BI Platform Engineer is responsible for the architecture, administration, scalability, and governance of the enterprise Power BI and Microsoft Fabric ecosystem. Rather than focusing solely on building visual dashboards, this role operates under a platform-engineering mindset—treating BI infrastructure as a managed product. You will oversee workspace design, premium capacity/Fabric capacity management, data refresh optimization, enterprise-scale gateway architectures, and CI/CD deployment pipelines. Working at the intersection of BI developers, enterprise data platform teams, and governance bodies, you ensure high availability, data security, performance standards, and cost-efficient capacity utilization across the entire organization.

Responsibilities

* Tenant Administration & Platform Governance: Manage Power BI tenant settings, capacity configurations, licensing allocation, and organizational governance policies. Implement best practices for workspace lifecycles, access control, and workspace domain hierarchies.
* Capacity & Performance Optimization: Monitor and tune Fabric/Power BI capacities (F-SKUs and P-SKUs) using Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics. Identify memory throttling, CPU spikes, and query timeouts, partnering with semantic model developers to resolve bottlenecks.
* Enterprise Gateway Management: Architect, configure, patch, and monitor high-availability On-Premises Data Gateway clusters to ensure resilient hybrid connectivity to on-prem data warehouses and private network endpoints.
* CI/CD & DevOps Automation: Build and standardize automated release management using Power BI Deployment Pipelines, Fabric Git integration (Azure DevOps / GitHub), and PowerShell/Fabric REST APIs for automated deployments, regression checks, and model backups.
* Security & Compliance: Implement data protection policies including Microsoft Purview Information Protection sensitivity labels, Row-Level Security (RLS) / Object-Level Security (OLS) audit frameworks, and private endpoint / VNet data connectivity.
* Semantic Layer & Data Architecture Enablement: Guide enterprise teams on best practices for large-scale semantic models (Direct Lake, DirectQuery, composite models, XMLA read/write endpoints, and incremental refresh).
* Platform Operations & Support: Serve as the senior technical escalation point for platform-level outages, gateway failures, data refresh disruptions, and tenant misconfigurations.

Requirements

* Experience: 3–6 years of dedicated experience in enterprise BI administration, platform engineering, or enterprise analytics engineering with an emphasis on Power BI / Microsoft Fabric.
* Power BI & Fabric Administration: Deep practical knowledge of the Power BI Admin Portal, capacity resource allocation, tenant settings, and Fabric artifacts (Lakehouses, Warehouses, Semantic Models).
* Scripting & Automation: Strong scripting capabilities using PowerShell (MicrosoftPowerBIMgmt module) and Python, alongside familiarity with the Power BI REST APIs and Fabric Admin APIs.
* Data Connectivity & Networking: Hands-on experience deploying and load-balancing On-Premises Data Gateways, understanding network routing, service principals, Azure VNets, and private links.
* Semantic Modeling & Optimization: Advanced knowledge of tabular models, DAX query performance tuning, and tools like DAX Studio, Tabular Editor (BIML/TOM), and ALM Toolkit.
* DevOps & Version Control: Experience establishing Git-integrated developer workflows, deployment pipelines, and environment management (Dev/Test/Prod) in Azure DevOps or GitHub.
* Security Standards: Working knowledge of Azure Active Directory (Microsoft Entra ID), conditional access, service principals, RLS/OLS, and enterprise data masking principles.

Nice to Have

* Microsoft Fabric Unified Architecture: Early adoption or production exposure to Fabric core workloads (Synapse Data Engineering, Real-Time Intelligence, OneLake shortcuts).
* Cloud Data Warehousing: Operational experience interfacing with modern data platforms such as Snowflake, Azure Databricks, or Google BigQuery.
* Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Experience provisioning Azure analytics resources and gateway machines via Terraform or Bicep/ARM templates.
* Certifications: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate (DP-600) or Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300).
* Cost Engineering: Experience designing internal chargeback models and usage attribution frameworks for multi-tenant BI capacities.

title: L2 Engineer - Platform & Agentic Ops
description:
About the Role

The L2 Engineer – Platform & Agentic Ops bridges core infrastructure operations, platform reliability, and autonomous AI agent operations (Agentic Ops). In this intermediate role, you act as the operational backbone for enterprise platforms hosting microservices, data workflows, and multi-agent AI systems. You will handle escalations from Level 1 support, diagnose platform anomalies, trace AI agent execution failures (e.g., tool-call loops, prompt regressions, and token overruns), and maintain high availability across cloud environments. This position works closely with Platform, DevOps, and AI/ML Engineering teams to automate runbooks, optimize agentic workflows, and maintain platform stability.

Responsibilities

* Agentic Ops & Telemetry Analysis: Monitor autonomous AI agents and execution runtimes. Debug multi-step agent workflows, handle failed tool calls/function calling, resolve context-window and token budget limits, and mitigate runaway loops or infinite retry chains.
* Platform Operations & Incident Management: Serve as an escalation point (L2) for production incidents, service degradations, and system alerts across Kubernetes clusters, API gateways, and cloud infrastructure.
* Observability & Distributed Tracing: Instrument and monitor end-to-end telemetry across both traditional infrastructure and LLM/agent pipelines (inspecting spans from prompt $\rightarrow$ routing $\rightarrow$ retrieval $\rightarrow$ tool execution).
* Automation & Runbook Engineering: Convert repetitive manual fixes into automated scripts, self-healing jobs, or standardized Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to empower L1 teams.
* Cost & Quota Governance: Track, manage, and enforce rate limits, model routing thresholds, and API credit/token consumption across foundation model providers and vector databases.
* CI/CD & Deployment Support: Assist in deploying, validating, and rolling back platform services, prompt configurations, agent definitions, and model gateway updates safely.
* Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Partner with L3/core engineering teams on detailed post-mortems for major platform or agentic pipeline failures.

Requirements

* Experience: 2–4 years in Systems Support, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevOps, or Platform Operations.
* Scripting & Programming: Proficiency in Python (essential for agent runtimes and automations) or Bash/Go/Node.js.
* Cloud & Containerization: Practical experience operating and debugging within containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes) on major cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
* Agentic & LLM Fundamentals: Foundational understanding of how LLMs and agent frameworks function—including tool/function calling, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), embeddings, context window management, and prompt handling.
* Observability Stack: Hands-on experience with logging, metric, and tracing tools (e.g., Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK).
* Networking & APIs: Solid grasp of REST APIs, gRPC, JSON schemas, webhooks, authentication (OAuth/IAM), and HTTP status debugging.
* Problem-Solving & Communication: Clear documentation skills, disciplined troubleshooting under SLA constraints, and effective cross-functional communication.

Nice to Have

* Agentic Framework Exposure: Direct operational experience with frameworks like LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or Semantic Kernel.
* LLM Tracing & Evaluation Tools: Familiarity with LLM observability tools such as LangSmith, Phoenix (Arize), Langfuse, or Weights & Biases.
* Vector Databases: Operational familiarity with vector stores (e.g., Pinecone, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma, pgvector).
* Workflow Orchestrators: Exposure to durable execution engines or workflow tools (e.g., Temporal, Airflow, Prefect).
* Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Basic knowledge of Terraform or Helm for managing platform components.
* Certifications: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator / Solutions Architect Associate, CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator), or cloud AI certifications.

title: L1 Engineer - Platform Engineering
description:
About the Role

The L1 Engineer – Platform Engineering serves as the front-line guardian of platform reliability, developer tooling, and core infrastructure health. In this entry- to associate-level role, you are the first point of contact for software engineers needing platform support and the first responder to automated alerts across cloud environments, CI/CD pipelines, and shared internal developer platforms (IDP). Working within standard operating procedures (SOPs) and runbooks, you triage incoming requests, resolve known environment failures, monitor health dashboards, and escalate complex issues smoothly to L2 and platform architects. This role offers an accelerated pathway into DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), and cloud platform architecture.

Responsibilities

* First-Response Incident Management: Monitor real-time platform alerts, health dashboards, and synthetic checks
* triage incoming incident tickets and act quickly to restore services following documented runbooks.
* Developer Platform Support: Assist product and application teams with developer onboarding, service catalog access, namespace provisioning, and permissions (RBAC) across shared platform clusters.

title: BI & Semantic Model Engineer
description:
About the Role

The BI & Semantic Model Engineer serves as the critical bridge between raw data lakehouses/warehouses and business intelligence consumers. In this role, you design, build, and optimize governed, enterprise-grade semantic layers that translate complex distributed data schemas into intuitive, performant business models. Rather than simply building front-end charts, you focus on data modeling rigor, calculation design, query performance optimization, and self-service enablement. You will establish single-source-of-truth metric definitions, implement granular security policies (RLS/OLS), and optimize high-throughput analytics pipelines across enterprise BI platforms (such as Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Cube, or dbt Semantic Layer) and modern cloud data warehouses.

Responsibilities

* Enterprise Semantic Modeling: Architect, build, and maintain centralized tabular semantic models, dimensional models (star/snowflake schemas), and universal metrics layers that serve disparate business units and analytical workloads.
* Calculation & Metric Standardization: Develop, test, and document complex business logic, KPIs, time-intelligence calculations, and metric definitions using advanced analytical languages (DAX, MDX, or semantic engine code like Cube.js / MetricFlow).
* Performance Tuning & Storage Engine Optimization: Optimize query response times, compression, memory footprints, and partition schemes. Transition high-volume datasets across optimal storage modes (Direct Lake, In-Memory/Import, DirectQuery, Aggregations, and Composite models).
* Tooling & Code-First Lifecycle Management: Maintain semantic models as code using developer tooling (Tabular Editor, ALM Toolkit, dbt, or BIML). Manage schema migrations, metadata versioning, and CI/CD deployment pipelines using Git and Azure DevOps/GitHub.
* Security & Governance Architecture: Design and enforce data governance protocols, including dynamic Row-Level Security (RLS), Object-Level Security (OLS), data masking, and sensitivity labels across shared datasets.
* Data Integration & Transformation: Collaborate with Data Engineers to shape raw lakehouse/warehouse schemas (Snowflake, Databricks, Fabric Lakehouse, BigQuery) into analytics-ready curated views and facts/dimensions.
* Auditing & Query Diagnostics: Profile slow-running reports, identify inefficient query execution plans using DAX Studio or database query profilers, and tune relationship cardinalities, filter context evaluation, and materialized aggregates.

Requirements

* Experience: 3–6 years of dedicated experience in enterprise BI engineering, data modeling, or analytics engineering with a primary focus on semantic layer architecture.Advanced Semantic Modeling & DAX: Deep technical mastery of tabular modeling engines, star schemas, bidirectional filtering nuances, and writing efficient, highly performant DAX calculations and window functions.Data Warehousing & SQL Mastery: Exceptional SQL skills for complex data querying, transformation, window functions, and designing optimal dimensional schemas ($Kimball$ methodology).Cloud Data Platforms: Production experience sourcing data from cloud data warehouses/lakehouses such as Snowflake, Azure Synapse / Fabric, Databricks (Delta Lake), or Google BigQuery.Model Engineering Tooling: Hands-on experience with modern semantic developer tools like Tabular Editor 2/3, DAX Studio, and Git-integrated BI deployment workflows.Storage Modes & Data Refresh Architecture: Working knowledge of optimizing incremental refreshes, hybrid partitions, DirectQuery caching limits, and modern engine features like Direct Lake on Delta Parquet files.Data Governance & Security: Proven track record implementing scalable dynamic security frameworks (RLS/OLS) driven by Active Directory/Entra ID groups or custom entitlement tables.

Nice to Have

* Universal Semantic Layers: Experience with headless or universal semantic layer tools (e.g., Cube, dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow, GoodData, or AtScale).
* Scripting & Automation: Proficiency in Python or PowerShell for programmatic model management (e.g., using Tabular Object Model / TOM, PyPowerBI, or Semantic Link / SemPy).
* XMLA / API Operations: Familiarity with script-based dataset management via XMLA endpoints, TMSL (Tabular Model Scripting Language), or Fabric/Power BI REST APIs.
* Modern Orchestration: Familiarity with data transform orchestration tools such as dbt Core/Cloud, Apache Airflow, or Fabric Data Factory.
* Certifications: Microsoft Certified: Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate (DP-600), Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300), or SnowPro Core Certification.

You will act as the primary operational liaison between external enterprise customers and internal engineering organizations. * Customer Relationship & Escalation Handling: Serve as the designated operational escalation contact for enterprise customer stakeholders. Manage client friction, track recurring customer pain points, and translate operational findings into feature requests for the product roadmap.
* Vendor & Tooling Operations: Oversee support tools and platforms, including ITSM systems (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management), paging systems (PagerDuty, Opsgenie), and client-facing status portals.

Requirements

title: UI Architect
description:
**About Ginesys**

Ginesys is India's leading retail technology platform, powering 1,200+ customers and 50,000+ users through the unified GinesysOne suite — ERP, Cloud POS (Zwing), Order Management (Browntape), GST Compliance (EaseMyGST), and BI (InsightX). We are evolving from a System of Records to a System of Intelligence through Ginesys.AI.

**Role Summary**

The UI Architect is the single accountable owner of enterprise UI architecture across all products. This person defines the design system, reusable foundation layer, and UI governance model that every product team builds on — enabling consistent, scalable, and intuitive experiences across ERP, POS, OMS, WMS, Reporting, and future modules.

This is a matrix leadership role. The UI Architect does not own product-specific design decisions or engineering implementation — those stay with Product Managers and Engineering respectively. Instead, this role sets the standards, patterns, and governance those decisions must work within, and partners closely with Product Management, Engineering, and Customer Success to apply them.

This is a hands-on architecture and design leadership role. The person doesn't just define standards on paper — they build reusable component libraries, foundation screens, and research-backed patterns that product teams consume directly.

**What This Role Owns**

* **Enterprise UI/UX architecture:** the long-term design architecture strategy across all products.
* **Enterprise Design System:** tokens, typography, color, spacing, grid, components, patterns, accessibility, and responsive standards — owned and evolved centrally.
* **UI Foundation Layer:** reusable screens and patterns (auth, navigation, dashboards, tables, forms, filters, notifications, empty / loading / error states) that every product consumes.
* **Design capability building:** mentoring UI developers and leads and guiding front-end engineers on usability principles.

**What This Role Does Not Own**

* **Product roadmap or feature prioritization:** owned by Product Managers.
* **Product-specific UX decisions:** co-owned with Product Managers within the enterprise design system — this role sets the standards, Product Managers decide the product's specific workflows.
* **Engineering implementation and technology stack decisions:** owned by Engineering Architects; this role ensures designs are aligned with and feasible on the chosen stack.
* **People management of designers embedded in product teams:** reporting model to be confirmed with leadership.
* **Brand identity and marketing collateral:** owned by Marketing/Brand, where such a function exists; this role ensures product UX stays brand-compliant.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Enterprise UI/UX Architecture**

* Define the long-term UI architecture strategy across all products and own the scalable enterprise design framework.
* Establish standardized UI principles, reusable interaction models, navigation frameworks, and common user journeys for enterprise workflows.
* Define information architecture standards and a scalable component taxonomy that enables rapid product development.

**UI Foundation Layer**

* Architect and standardize a reusable UI foundation layer — authentication, navigation, search, dashboards, notifications, tables/data grids, forms, filters, pagination, reports, wizards, dialogs, and standard empty/loading/error/success states.
* Ensure this foundation reduces implementation effort for every future product and module.

**Product-Specific UX Partnership**

* Partner with Product Managers to design differentiated experiences for ERP, POS, OMS, WMS, Inventory, Finance, Reporting, and AI-enabled workflows.
* Translate business workflows into intuitive digital experiences within the enterprise design system.

**Technology Alignment**

* Collaborate with Engineering Architects to ensure designs align with the technology stack and are technically scalable.
* Partner with engineering teams through implementation to protect design intent.

**Matrix Collaboration And Leadership**

* Work across Product Management, Engineering, Customer Support, Customer Success, Sales, and Implementation teams — influencing without direct authority.
* Mentor UI developers, guide front-end engineers, and conduct design workshops to build organizational design capability.

**Continuous Innovation**

* Track industry trends (AI-powered UX, conversational interfaces, design automation, micro-frontends, cross-platform design) and recommend adoption where it strengthens the enterprise experience.

14+ years in UI design and architecture, including at least 5+ years leading enterprise design systems.

Experience architecting UI across multiple products in an enterprise SaaS organization.

Deep expertise in design systems, accessibility standards, and interaction pattern architecture.

Strong front-end technical fluency (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript/TypeScript, React/Angular/Vue) to credibly partner with engineering.

Experience running UI governance — design reviews, quality gates, and pattern library management.

Experience operating in a matrix organization — influencing Product, Engineering, and Customer Success without direct authority.

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, or a related discipline; Master's degree preferred.

**Helpful Experience**

Retail domain experience — POS, ERP, Order Management, Warehouse Management, Omnichannel Retail, e-commerce, or Supply Chain.

Experience with the specific design and front-end tooling in use (Figma, FigJam, Storybook, design tokens, micro-frontend architecture).

Exposure to AI-enabled product experiences and conversational interfaces.

Experience working with globally distributed product and engineering teams.

We go out of our way to retain the small business feeling with which we started and stimulate innovation and collaboration through teamwork and our non-hierarchical approach.
